ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the angle bisectors of $ \angle ABC$ and $\angle ACB$ intersect at point F. A line through F is drawn parallel to $BC$, intersecting $AB$ at point D and $AC$ at point E. Given that $BD = 3\,cm$ and $EC = 2\,cm$, what is the length of $DE$ in centimeters?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $BF$ is the bisector of $\angle ABC$,\\
it follows that $\angle DBF=\angle CBF$,\\
Since $DE \parallel BC$,\\
it then implies $\angle DFB=\angle CBF$,\\
Thus, $\angle DBF=\angle DFB$,\\
Hence, $DF=BD=3\, cm$,\\
Similarly, it can be concluded that $EF=EC=2\, cm$,\\
Therefore, $DE=DF+EF=\boxed{5\, cm}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the angle bisectors of $ \angle ABC$ and $\angle ACB$ intersect at point F. A line through F is drawn parallel to $BC$, intersecting $AB$ at point D and $AC$ at point E. Given that $BD = 3\,cm$ and $EC = 2\,cm$, what is the length of $DE$ in centimeters?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $BF$ is the bisector of $\angle ABC$,\\
it follows that $\angle DBF=\angle CBF$,\\
Since $DE \parallel BC$,\\
it then implies $\angle DFB=\angle CBF$,\\
Thus, $\angle DBF=\angle DFB$,\\
Hence, $DF=BD=3\, cm$,\\
Similarly, it can be concluded that $EF=EC=2\, cm$,\\
Therefore, $DE=DF+EF=\boxed{5\, cm}$

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is triangle ABC, with BC as the horizontal base, and A above. Point D is on side AB, point E is on side AC, point F is inside the triangle, and D, F, E are on the same horizontal line; this line is parallel to BC. The figure also draws BF and CF, which are respectively the angle bisectors starting from B and C. It is known that BD = 3 cm, EC = 2 cm. Then reason: By the coordinate method, put BC on the x-axis, and let the line passing through F and parallel to BC be y = r. Let ∠ABC = 2β, then BF is the angle bisector, so the angle between BF and BC is β, while the angle between AB and BC is 2β. Point D is on AB and has height r, therefore BD = r csc(2β). Point F is on BF and has height r, point D is on AB and has height r, so DF = r(cot β - cot 2β). Using the identity cot β - cot 2β = csc(2β), get DF = r csc(2β) = BD = 3 cm. Similarly, let ∠ACB = 2γ, because CF is the angle bisector, one can get EF = EC = 2 cm. In the figure F is located between D and E, therefore DE = DF + EF = 3 + 2 = 5 cm.
